summary: Modern databases are increasingly embedding AI/ML capabilities directly into the data platform, eliminating the need to move data to separate ML systems for inference, embedding generation, and semantic search. Vector search has become a defining feature, with adoption growing 377% year-over-year and an estimated 75% of enterprise AI applications expected to depend on vector search by 2026. The key differentiators now are native vector indexing, in-database LLM access, and governance over the data being embedded and retrieved.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (serverless LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, Document AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to LLMs and task-specific functions (SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, COMPLETE, EMBED_TEXT) directly via SQL and Python, alongside Cortex Search for RAG and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying. With the 2025 launch of Snowflake Postgres, these AI capabilities extend to a managed Postgres service unified with Snowflake analytics and the Horizon Catalog for governance.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a built-in VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions and Cortex Search for managed hybrid vector + keyword retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Native in-platform LLMs via Cortex (hosted models such as Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, and Snowflake Arctic) callable from SQL/Python; no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex functions billed per token/credit consumed by model and compute. No separate ML platform license required.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (in-SQL model training) + Vertex AI integration + BigQuery vector/text/hybrid search
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, forecasting, clustering) using standard SQL, while Vertex AI integration enables calling Gemini and other foundation models for generation and embeddings. BigQuery also offers graph analytics, embedding generation, and RAG-style retrieval directly in the warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides built-in vector search with the VECTOR_SEARCH function and vector indexes, supporting vector, text, and hybrid search without third-party tools.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Vertex AI / Gemini models invoked via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING SQL functions; also supports remote models and external endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-per-query (on-demand bytes scanned) or capacity-based slot pricing; AI inference and embedding incur additional Vertex AI model usage charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector (vector storage/search extension) + pgai (in-database embedding and LLM workflows)
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds vector columns and similarity search, while pgai (from Timescale) brings embedding generation and LLM calls into SQL. Snowflake's own developer guidance highlights keeping vectors, relational data, and semantic search together in Postgres to avoid separate systems.
databases.vector_search_notes: Extension-based but first-class. Vector search in PostgreSQL requires the pgvector extension (not in the base engine). It is open source, widely adopted, and supports HNSW and IVFFlat indexes, so it is effectively 'native-grade' when installed — but it is technically an extension rather than core engine functionality.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai and related extensions, PostgreSQL can call external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama, etc.) from SQL; no built-in hosted models in the core engine.
databases.pricing_notes: Free and open source; cost is infrastructure/hosting plus any external LLM API usage. Managed providers (e.g., Snowflake Postgres, Timescale, Supabase, RDS) add their own service pricing.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (in-database inference via SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock/Comprehend integration)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML predictions directly from SQL by integrating Aurora with Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon Comprehend, returning model outputs as query results without building custom pipelines. It is aimed at enriching transactional data with predictions and generative outputs in place.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively built into Aurora ML. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is achieved via the pgvector extension, which is a third-party/community extension rather than a native Aurora ML capability; therefore marked false for native built-in vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and Comprehend via SQL functions (e.g., aws_ml / aws_bedrock), plus SageMaker-hosted custom models.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora instance/storage/IO pricing plus separate charges for invoked SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend services; no bundled ML license.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (create/train/predict models in SQL via SageMaker Autopilot and Bedrock integration)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data warehouse users to create and train ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, automatically leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot, and to run in-warehouse predictions at scale. It also integrates with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI functions over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not a core Redshift ML feature. Redshift has introduced vector/embedding support primarily through Bedrock integration and limited vector functions, but native, general-purpose built-in vector indexing comparable to dedicated vector databases is not a standard Redshift ML capability; marked false and best handled via external vector stores or OpenSearch.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock (and SageMaker) to run generative AI and embedding functions over warehouse data through SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute (RPU/node) and storage pricing plus underlying SageMaker training/Bedrock inference costs charged separately.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI stack through Mosaic AI, covering foundation model serving, fine-tuning, agent frameworks, and MLflow-based lifecycle management, all governed by Unity Catalog. Databricks Vector Search delivers managed, governance-aware vector indexes synced from Delta tables for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed service that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables and supports hybrid (vector + keyword) retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Native Foundation Model APIs and Mosaic AI Model Serving host open and proprietary LLMs; supports external model routing and agent/RAG orchestration within the lakehouse.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based DBU pricing across compute, model serving, and vector search; foundation model inference billed per token or provisioned throughput.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search + Atlas Search for semantic and hybrid retrieval
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search stores embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and performs approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search within the same database, enabling RAG and semantic search without a separate vector store. It integrates with popular AI frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and supports hybrid full-text plus vector queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability of MongoDB Atlas using HNSW-based approximate nearest-neighbor indexing on vector fields within collections.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face) and AI frameworks to generate embeddings and power RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Included within Atlas cluster pricing (compute/storage tiers); vector search uses dedicated or shared Search Nodes that may add cost. Based on cluster resource consumption.
